behavioral_effects: The frontend has a typed ES-import graph: 359 modules, 867 edges, zero unresolved specifiers, zero unreadable files, one opaque dynamic-import site (i18n.ts locale loader). Session 6.5 can now walk import chains on both sides of the proxy.
The regex-vs-parser decision has a standing evidence gate: a real-tree test fails if the unresolved rate reaches 2 percent, naming a parser as the remedy.
compatibility_impact: None. Reuses the existing ImportGraph container and edge vocabulary; no generated output or schema changed, and sync moved zero bytes.
follow_up: Session 6.3 extracts route, task, model, test, and tool relations; 6.4 stores all graphs in the SQLite cache.
limitations: The graph is built and tested but not yet consumed: impact analysis still ignores frontend paths until session 6.5 wires the cross-language expansion.
reason: Impact analysis is blind on the frontend side: hist-new-chat-new-conversation misses half its expected validators because nothing can follow an import chain through frontend/src, so the cross-language expansion in session 6.5 has no graph to walk; this adds the typed ES-import graph with the same uncertainty contract as the Python one
risks: Bare baseUrl specifiers (src/lib/x without the @ alias) would be misread as package imports; the codebase does not use them and the unresolved-rate gate is the tripwire if that changes.
rollback: git revert of the single commit; the extractor has no callers yet outside its tests.
security_impact: None. Read-only extraction over frontend/src; no permission, exposure, or runtime path changed.
